Create a GlycoproteomicSE object

Source: R/glyco-se.R, R/se-names.R
GlycoproteomicSE.Rd

GlycoproteomicSE() creates a single-assay SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment() subclass for glycoproteomics data. It is a thin wrapper around SummarizedExperiment() with additional Glycoverse validation:

  1. Exactly one assay is allowed. Extra assays are rejected to avoid ambiguous glycoproteomics measurements.

  2. The assay must contain only non-negative values when scale is "raw". Negative values are allowed for "log", "log2", "log10", and "logx" scales.

  3. rowData must contain protein, protein_site, and glycan_composition columns. The protein column must be character, protein_site must be integer-like, and glycan_composition must be a glyrepr::glycan_composition() vector. A glycan_structure column is optional, but if present it must be a glyrepr::glycan_structure() vector.

  4. metadata must contain a glycan_type field.

This container is experimental and is not recognized by all Glycoverse packages yet. It is intended to become a recommended entry point as package contracts migrate toward SummarizedExperiment-based containers.

Usage

GlycoproteomicSE(abundance, ...)

# S4 method for class 'GlycoproteomicSE,list'
dimnames(x) <- value

# S4 method for class 'GlycoproteomicSE,NULL'
dimnames(x) <- value

# S4 method for class 'GlycoproteomicSE'
rownames(x) <- value

# S4 method for class 'GlycoproteomicSE'
colnames(x) <- value

Arguments

abundance

A numeric abundance matrix with glycopeptides or glycoforms as rows and samples as columns.

...

Arguments passed to SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment().

  • rowData: A S4Vectors::DataFrame() with at least the following columns:

    • protein: required, a character vector

    • protein_site: required, an integer-like vector

    • glycan_composition: required, a glyrepr::glycan_composition() vector

    • glycan_structure: optional, a glyrepr::glycan_structure() vector

  • colData: A S4Vectors::DataFrame().

  • metadata: A list. It must include a glycan_type field with one of "N", "O", "O-GalNAc", "O-Man", "O-Fuc", "O-GlcNAc", "O-Glc", "HMO", "GSL", "GAG", "GPI", or "others". The optional scale field is "raw" (original linear scale, the default) or "log" (natural logarithm), "log2", "log10", or "logx". "logx" denotes a transformed logarithmic or log-like analysis scale (for example, CLR, ALR, or VSN) whose original abundance cannot be inferred or restored automatically from scale alone. It does not imply a common mathematical interpretation or log2 fold changes. This field describes the supplied data; setting it does not transform the assay or migrate existing objects.

x

A GlycoproteomicSE object whose names are replaced.

value

Replacement names, or a two-element list for dimnames<-.

Value

A GlycoproteomicSE object.

Details

Older development objects used "log" without specifying a base. Update their metadata to "log2" or "log10" if that was the transformation applied. Constructors never infer the base or transform abundance values.

S4 class

GlycoproteomicSE is an S4 class that extends SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment().

Row and column names

Rows (variables) and columns (samples) are handled independently. Supplied names must be complete (no NA or empty strings) and unique within each axis. When abundance and the corresponding annotation table both have names, their name sets must match exactly; rowData or colData is reordered to match abundance, without reordering the abundance values. When only one component has names, the other inherits them by position. When neither has names, variable names are generated as V1, V2, ... and sample names as S1, S2, ... . Annotation tables must have the corresponding number of rows.

We recommend supplying matching names on all three components whenever possible: row and column names on abundance, variable row names on rowData, and sample row names on colData. This lets the constructor detect missing or mismatched identities early; a different order is aligned automatically. Omitted names remain supported through the inheritance and generation rules. Ordinary variable and sample annotation columns are not identity keys.

The resolved names are stored on the object, annotation tables, and underlying assay. Even assay(x, withDimnames = FALSE) has the resolved names. The checkDimnames argument cannot disable these naming rules. Replacing names with rownames<-, colnames<-, or dimnames<- requires complete, unique names of the correct length and synchronizes the underlying assay without moving abundance values or annotations. Use the conversion helpers to normalize names on an older object; duplicates or incomplete supplied names must be corrected explicitly before conversion.
